claims: Skip-on-fail schedule volume and output are defined for finite lists of CPMM intents.
For equal-input intents, the pool state after two executions is order-invariant.
Adding one prior equal-input execution can reduce tail schedule volume by at most one lot size.
For equal-input intents ordered by descending minOut, an adjacent greedy order has at least the schedule volume of the swapped order.
For two equal-input intents, total output and surplus are order-invariant when both execute.
Position output through repeated equal-input execution is non-increasing across arbitrary offsets.
Satisfiability at a later equal-input position implies satisfiability at the earlier position.
Schedule volume is bounded by the sum of offered inputs.
proof_method: structural recursion over finite intent lists
position-output monotonicity through repeated equal-input CPMM depletion
native witnesses for non-vacuity and sharpness examples
